summary: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Cornell University. He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director around 1969 to 1989, and has served as chairman of the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya worked in philosophy and Indology, earning a B.A. from the University of Calcutta and studying under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (circa 1943–1973) and served as a visiting professor at Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. She completed a PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and a Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the chair in Asian art history (1994–2015).

Deborah Sutton is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD in modern history at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1997–2001) and was attested in 2026 as Professor in Modern South Asian History at Lancaster University.
Declan Quigley is a scholar in Indology and other fields. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Renmin University of China, where he was attested in 2005 as an associate professor of religious studies.

Deepak Sarma works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Reed College and the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow and Gerald James Larson, and became Professor of Religious Studies at Case Western Reserve University around 2004.

Deepro Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who earned a B.A. from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MPhil from Jawaharlal Nehru University, and a PhD from the University of Alberta. He served as assistant professor at Gurudas College from 2014 to 2017.
Delphine Menant worked in Indology and religious studies and studied under James Darmesteter. In 1900, she served as chargée de mission dans l'Inde for the Guimet Museum.
Demchok Dorje was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington as director (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge, and held the Chair of Chinese at both the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980).

Denise Bernot was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, studying at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He served as principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (circa 1978–1986) and abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991).

Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes in 2012, later working at Vienna's South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library.

Dennis Genpo Merzel is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California and its Rossier School of Education, and trained under Taizan Maezumi from circa 1972 to 1995.

Dennis Hirota works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of California, Berkeley and Nagoya University, holding professorships at Chikushi Jogakuen University (circa 1992–1996) and Ryukoku University (2014).
Denys de Saumarez Bray was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (circa 1894–1898). He served as a member of the Council of India from 1930 to 1937.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji from 1946 to 1949. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (1961–1987) and Iryo Sosei University (1989–1995).
Denzil Ibbetson worked in Indology and other fields. He completed his education at St Peter's College, Adelaide, and at St John's College, where he earned a B.A. in mathematics between 1865 and 1869.
